name: SearchJetEngine – Instant Search for WordPress & WooCommerce
author: Maidul

sections.description:
Install SearchJet and your site’s search box starts showing matching products and pages while visitors type, with photos, prices and stock. There is nothing to set up: it works the moment you activate it.

Instant search as you type

A live dropdown appears under your search box with the best matches: product photo, title, price, category and stock status. Visitors find what they want without waiting for a results page.

WooCommerce product search

Shoppers can find products by name, SKU, variation SKU, category, tag and product attribute (size, colour, material). Exact title and SKU matches come first. Out-of-stock and hidden products are handled the way your store is set up.

Search by SKU and product code

Type a product code and the matching product comes first, including variations. Useful for stores whose customers search by part number.

A better search results page

Turn on one switch and SearchJet also powers the page visitors see after pressing Enter, with the same photos and prices. Leave it off and your theme’s results page stays as it is.

Works with your theme

SearchJet attaches to your theme’s existing search boxes by itself, on desktop and on phones. You can also place a box anywhere with the [searchjet_form] shortcode.

You choose what can be found

Pick which content types are searchable (posts, pages, products and more). Only published, public content that is not password-protected is ever returned.

Your design, your colours

Set colours, font size and borders, and choose what each result shows (thumbnail, price, category, excerpt, stock). The preview uses your own products.

Light on your site

Answers are cached, searches are rate-limited per visitor, and if anything goes wrong visitors simply see your theme’s own search results.

Typo-tolerant search (Cloud Mode)

Connect a free SearchJetEngine account and “hoddie” still finds the hoodies: small spelling mistakes no longer mean “no results”.

Search statistics (Cloud Mode)

See what visitors search for, which searches found nothing, and which results nobody clicked, with a weekly email of the top missed searches.

Search off your server (Cloud Mode)

With Cloud Mode the search engine runs on SearchJetEngine’s servers, so large catalogs add no load to your site.

Search by meaning (Cloud Mode, paid plans)

Find products by what shoppers mean, not only the exact words they type.

Cloud Mode is optional and has a free plan. SearchJet works fully without it, and you can switch it on or off any time under SearchJet > Settings.

Getting started

  1. Activate the plugin.
  2. Open SearchJet > Overview and type a product name in the “Try it” box.
  3. Visit your site and use the search box. That’s it.

Watch the 79-second demo: a shopper’s typo (“hoddie”) finds the right products, SKU search, and a product edit that updates search when you save.

Learn more

  • Live search demo
  • SearchJetEngine for WordPress and for WooCommerce
  • Documentation

External services

Only if you choose to connect an optional SearchJetEngine account. By default the plugin makes no request to any external service.

When you click Connect and approve the site (or save an API key), the plugin uses SearchJetEngine (https://app.searchjetengine.com, run by Dynamic Web Lab) to build the search index, answer searches and show statistics. It then sends your site’s public content (title, content, URL, author display name, images, categories, tags, language, product SKU, price and stock) when you index and when you publish, update or delete content, and what visitors type in the search box. Search and click statistics (search text, result count, page, browser user agent, session id) are also sent; the plugin does not send visitors’ IP addresses. Password-protected and non-public content is never sent. You can disconnect at any time under SearchJet > Settings.

Terms of use: https://searchjetengine.com/terms-of-use/
Privacy policy: https://searchjetengine.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/searchjet-instant-search directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin. Search works on the next page load.
  3. Open SearchJet > Overview to try it, and SearchJet > Search UI to change colours and what each result shows.
sections.faq:
Do I need an account?

No. SearchJet works as soon as you activate it. The free SearchJetEngine account (Cloud Mode) is optional and adds typo tolerance, search statistics and search off your server.

Does it work with WooCommerce?

Yes. Products are found by name, SKU (variation SKUs too), category, tag and attribute, and appear with price, stock and image.

Will it slow down my site?

It is built to stay light. Answers are cached for 60 seconds and one visitor is limited to 60 searches a minute. On catalogs with many thousands of products, the optional SearchJetEngine account moves search off your server.

Which content is searchable?

Public post types that your site includes in its own search: posts, pages, products and similar. Drafts, private, pending and scheduled items, password-protected posts, WooCommerce coupons and forms, and products hidden from search are never returned. Untick types under SearchJet > Settings.

Does it replace my theme’s search results page?

Only if you turn it on. The instant dropdown works out of the box; the results page is one switch on SearchJet > Overview.

What happens if I deactivate it?

Your theme’s search works as before, right away.

Does it support other languages?

Text is matched in any language. With WPML each post is stored with its language.

How is this different from Relevanssi, FiboSearch or SearchWP?

SearchJet focuses on the as-you-type experience: a fast dropdown with photos, prices and stock, SKU search, and a results page that matches. It works with no setup, and you can add an optional free account for typo tolerance.

Can I change the design?

Yes: colours, font size, borders and what each result shows, under SearchJet > Search UI.

What does it cost?

SearchJet is free. The optional SearchJetEngine account has a free plan and paid plans; see searchjetengine.com/pricing.
sections.changelog:
2.4.0

  • New: WordPress Mode, the new default. Search works the moment you activate the plugin, with no account: instant dropdown with photo, price, SKU, category and stock, matching titles, SKUs (variation SKUs too), categories, tags and attributes on your own site. Nothing is sent to anyone, no statistics are kept, and only published public content is returned. The search results page is yours to switch on. Typo tolerance, statistics and semantic search stay with Cloud Mode (a free SearchJetEngine account), and you can now disconnect at any time to go back to WordPress Mode.
  • Fix: before 2.4.0, a site that had not connected still sent each search a visitor typed to the SearchJetEngine service, which refused it. Nothing is sent before you connect any more.
  • New: a clearer admin. SearchJet > Overview shows whether search is live and lets you try it; Settings has Connect and Disconnect in one place; Analytics explains what a free account adds instead of showing an empty page; Search UI previews your own products instead of made-up ones; the floating help bubble is gone, and Indexing only appears in Cloud Mode.
  • Fix: Cloud Mode analytics showed made-up “sample” searches when there was no data. It now says there are no searches yet.
  • Privacy: clicks on search results no longer send the visitor’s IP address or the page they were on to the SearchJetEngine service. The service did not use them for clicks. Clicks that an older version left waiting to be sent lose those fields too.
  • Removed: the AI Agents page and the AI answers code. The SearchJetEngine service discontinued AI answers, and the AI Agents page never worked. Menu links, dashboard cards and plan text that mentioned them are gone; the plan FAQs in the admin no longer quote AI answer limits.
  • Fix: the progress of index-settings tasks now updates. The plugin asked the service at a URL that does not exist, and did not recognise the service’s “succeeded” status, so a finished task would have been checked again every 15 seconds for ever.
  • Fix: the “index completed” automation (webhook to n8n, Zapier or your own URL) now fires when a reindex finishes. It never fired before. The count is the number of documents sent in that run.
  • Fix: searches the plugin makes itself (the semantic-search check) always use the site’s public search key; the secret key is refused by the search service.
  • Readme: a new section, “Your data, in plain words”, answers what is sent, how long it is kept, whether other customers can see it, and how to delete it.

2.3.0

  • New: clicks are tied to the search that showed them. Your SearchJet dashboard can now list searches that found results nobody clicked, next to the zero-result searches. No setting to change.
  • New: when a search finds nothing exact, SearchJet now looks for a close match (a spelling fix from your own past searches, the meaningful words, or on Pro and higher the meaning). The dropdown and results page say so above the hits: “No results for … Showing results for …”.

2.2.4

  • New: a variation’s SKU finds its product. Searching “SHIRT-RED-M” shows the shirt it belongs to (up to 100 variation SKUs per product). Run a full reindex once (Indexing > Index Your Content) so existing variable products get them.
  • Fix: the instant dropdown now works in every product search box on the page, not only the first one. On themes with a separate search box for phones (Storefront and others), phone shoppers had no dropdown.
  • Fix: the dropdown waits for a short pause in typing before searching, so a typed phrase sends a few requests instead of one per key. This keeps shoppers under the search rate limit and uses fewer of your plan’s searches.
  • Fix: if a dropdown search fails, the dropdown closes instead of showing results for earlier text. A rate-limited search keeps what is shown and tries again.
  • Fix: if SearchJet has not answered within 3 seconds, the search results page shows your theme’s own results instead of staying blank.
  • Removed unused files from the plugin package (a 1.4 MB development cache and two unused PHP files).

2.2.3

  • New: WooCommerce product attributes are searchable: global attributes (Color, Size, …) and custom attributes set on a product. “red t-shirt” or “nike size 10” now finds products by their attribute values. Attributes hidden from the product page are not indexed, unless they are used for variations. Run a full reindex once (Indexing > Index Your Content) so existing products get their attributes.
  • New: semantic (AI) search on Pro, Growth and Enterprise plans: the instant dropdown and the search results page find products by what shoppers mean, not only by the exact words they type. Off by default: turn it on and set the balance on the Search UI page. If SearchJet does not allow it for the site, searches use keywords as before.

2.2.2

  • Fix: on multilingual (WPML/Polylang) sites, posts are now stored with the site’s own language code (for example “fr”, not “fr_FR” or the admin’s language), and the visitor’s current language is passed to search. The fallback search and AI answers no longer miss posts because of mismatched codes.
  • Polylang sites: run a full reindex once after updating (Indexing > Index Your Content) so stored language codes match.

2.2.1

  • Fix: a product (or post) moved to the trash, unpublished or made private now leaves search right away. Before, it stayed in the results.

  • Fix: WooCommerce changes made outside the product editor now reach search: price or stock changed through the REST API or an import, and a product that sells out through an order (it showed “In stock” until the next full reindex).
  • Fix: when SearchJet is busy (rate limit or a short outage), a product save or removal is retried in the background instead of being lost until the next full reindex.
  • The SearchJet admin pages ask the SearchJet API for account details far less often, so they no longer use up the site’s request limit.

short_description: Live instant search for WooCommerce and WordPress. Results as you type with photos, prices and stock. Search by SKU. Works on activation.
description:
Install SearchJet and your site’s search box starts showing matching products and pages while visitors type, with photos, prices and stock. There is nothing to set up: it works the moment you activate it.

Instant search as you type

A live dropdown appears under your search box with the best matches: product photo, title, price, category and stock status. Visitors find what they want without waiting for a results page.

WooCommerce product search

Shoppers can find products by name, SKU, variation SKU, category, tag and product attribute (size, colour, material). Exact title and SKU matches come first. Out-of-stock and hidden products are handled the way your store is set up.

Search by SKU and product code

Type a product code and the matching product comes first, including variations. Useful for stores whose customers search by part number.

A better search results page

Turn on one switch and SearchJet also powers the page visitors see after pressing Enter, with the same photos and prices. Leave it off and your theme’s results page stays as it is.

Works with your theme

SearchJet attaches to your theme’s existing search boxes by itself, on desktop and on phones. You can also place a box anywhere with the [searchjet_form] shortcode.

You choose what can be found

Pick which content types are searchable (posts, pages, products and more). Only published, public content that is not password-protected is ever returned.

Your design, your colours

Set colours, font size and borders, and choose what each result shows (thumbnail, price, category, excerpt, stock). The preview uses your own products.

Light on your site

Answers are cached, searches are rate-limited per visitor, and if anything goes wrong visitors simply see your theme’s own search results.

Typo-tolerant search (Cloud Mode)

Connect a free SearchJetEngine account and “hoddie” still finds the hoodies: small spelling mistakes no longer mean “no results”.

Search statistics (Cloud Mode)

See what visitors search for, which searches found nothing, and which results nobody clicked, with a weekly email of the top missed searches.

Search off your server (Cloud Mode)

With Cloud Mode the search engine runs on SearchJetEngine’s servers, so large catalogs add no load to your site.

Search by meaning (Cloud Mode, paid plans)

Find products by what shoppers mean, not only the exact words they type.

Cloud Mode is optional and has a free plan. SearchJet works fully without it, and you can switch it on or off any time under SearchJet > Settings.

Getting started

  1. Activate the plugin.
  2. Open SearchJet > Overview and type a product name in the “Try it” box.
  3. Visit your site and use the search box. That’s it.

Watch the 79-second demo: a shopper’s typo (“hoddie”) finds the right products, SKU search, and a product edit that updates search when you save.

Learn more

  • Live search demo
  • SearchJetEngine for WordPress and for WooCommerce
  • Documentation

External services

Only if you choose to connect an optional SearchJetEngine account. By default the plugin makes no request to any external service.

When you click Connect and approve the site (or save an API key), the plugin uses SearchJetEngine (https://app.searchjetengine.com, run by Dynamic Web Lab) to build the search index, answer searches and show statistics. It then sends your site’s public content (title, content, URL, author display name, images, categories, tags, language, product SKU, price and stock) when you index and when you publish, update or delete content, and what visitors type in the search box. Search and click statistics (search text, result count, page, browser user agent, session id) are also sent; the plugin does not send visitors’ IP addresses. Password-protected and non-public content is never sent. You can disconnect at any time under SearchJet > Settings.

Terms of use: https://searchjetengine.com/terms-of-use/
Privacy policy: https://searchjetengine.com/privacy
